function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Below is a quick‑look snapshot of some of the most widely‑publicised festivals that are scheduled to take place in the United States **after today’s date (2026‑10‑13)**.  The list is sorted by the first day of each event and includes a brief description, venue, and a link to the official website (where you can find the most up‑to‑date details, ticketing, and lineup information).

| # | Festival | Dates (2026) | Location | What to Expect | Official Site |
|---|----------|--------------|----------|----------------|---------------|
| 1 | **New York Comic Con** | Oct 13 – Oct 16 | New York City, NY | One of the largest pop‑culture conventions in the world. Panels, cosplay contests, exclusive previews of comics, movies, TV shows, and gaming. | <https://www.comic-con.org/new-york> |
| 2 | **Halloween** | Oct 31 | Nationwide (various local celebrations) | Traditional trick‑or‑treat, themed parties, haunted houses, and community events. Many cities host special “Halloween festivals” with music, food, and family‑friendly activities. | — |
| 3 | **Thanksgiving Day Parade** | Nov 24 | Washington, D.C. | The iconic parade featuring floats, marching bands, and the “Thanksgiving Day Parade” tradition. | <https://www.nationalparade.com> |
| 4 | **New York Film Festival** | Sep 27 – Oct 9 | New York City, NY | Premier film festival showcasing independent and international cinema. Screenings, Q&A sessions, and industry panels. | <https://www.nyff.org> |
| 5 | **Sundance Film Festival** | Jan 20 – Jan 29 | Park City, UT | The world’s premier independent film festival. Screenings, workshops, and networking events for filmmakers and audiences. | <https://www.sundance.org> |
| 6 | **SXSW (South by Southwest)** | Mar 11 – Mar 20 | Austin, TX | Multi‑disciplinary festival featuring music, film, interactive media, and tech. Panels, concerts, and startup showcases. | <https://www.sxsw.com> |
| 7 | **Coachella Valley Music & Arts Festival** | Apr 14 – Apr 16 | Indio, CA | One of the most famous music festivals in the world. Two weekends of top‑tier music, art installations, and celebrity sightings. | <https://www.coachella.com> |
| 8 | **New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival** | Apr 28 – May 1 | New Orleans, LA | Celebrates jazz, blues, and Creole music with street parades, live performances, and cultural exhibits. | <https://www.nojazzfest.com> |
| 9 | **Burning Man** | Aug 27 – Sep 4 | Black Rock Desert, NV | An experimental arts community that culminates in the burning of a large wooden effigy. Art installations, music, and communal living. | <https://burningman.org> |
|10 | **Lollapalooza** | Aug 4 – Aug 7 | Chicago, IL | Major music festival featuring rock, hip‑hop, electronic, and indie acts. | <https://www.lollapalooza.com> |

### How to Use This List

1. **Pick a festival that interests you** – whether it’s music, film, comics, or a holiday celebration.
2. **Visit the official website** linked above for the most current lineup, ticket prices, travel accommodations, and any COVID‑19 or safety guidelines.
3. **Plan ahead** – many festivals sell out months in advance, so book tickets and lodging early if you’re interested.

### Quick Tips

- **Travel & Accommodation**: Book flights and hotels at least 3–6 months in advance for major festivals like Coachella or SXSW.
- **Tickets**: Look for early‑bird specials or bundle packages (e.g., VIP + lodging).
- **Weather**: Check the forecast for the festival location. For example, Coachella is typically hot and dry, while Burning Man can be extremely dusty and hot.
- **Local Events**: Many cities host smaller, community‑run festivals on the same weekend (e.g., Halloween parades, Thanksgiving parades). These can be great for a more relaxed experience.

---

If you’re looking for a specific type of festival (e.g., food, tech, cultural, or niche music), let me know and I can narrow the list or add more details!
